checks.what: Rounded unit odds ratio with significance
checks.calculation: An odds ratio printed as 1.000 can differ from unity, and an SE printed as 0.000 can be strictly positive and small. The pair does not fix a Wald statistic or sign.
checks.rounding_interval_used: OR in [0.9995,1.0005]; SE in [0,0.0005], with positive SE needed for an ordinary Wald test.
checks.note: Do not erase the symbol or treat the interaction as exactly zero. This also prevents recovery of a precise quadratic time interaction for prediction.

checks.what: Table 6 zero-rounded SEs
checks.calculation: A printed 0.0000 SE permits a sufficiently small positive SE; the corresponding effects can be statistically significant.
checks.rounding_interval_used: SE in [0,0.00005]; each effect in printed value ±0.00005.
checks.note: No infinite test statistic is inferred from printed zero.

checks.what: Seven-point effect examples versus local derivatives
checks.calculation: Seven times the absolute printed local effect, expressed in percentage points, gives 2.73, 0.63, 24.64 and 24.71, matching the text.
checks.rounding_interval_used: Each derivative gives ±0.035 percentage points after multiplication by 700; each two-decimal percent has ±0.005 interval. Corresponding intervals intersect.
checks.note: Arithmetic matches a linear approximation. Percent likelihood changes in prose have no specified denominator; derivatives times seven do not establish relative percentages or exact finite changes. Total points also changes in a real touchdown scenario.

checks.what: Exact finite-change interpretation of seven-point examples
checks.calculation: Exact finite differences require probabilities at both endpoints, including intercept/fixed effects and every changed regressor. These are not supplied.
checks.rounding_interval_used: Rounded slope intervals do not determine endpoint probabilities; no central-value substitution is made.
checks.note: Separate a local approximation from an exact probability difference; do not insert reconstructed probabilities into targets.

checks.what: H1A shape and observed support after rounding
checks.calculation: The Model 2 below-branch index stationary point is -ln(OR_linear)/(2*ln(OR_quadratic)). Full OR intervals allow stationary points both within and below published support. Table 6 all-quarter derivatives do not themselves show a positive far-below slope.
checks.rounding_interval_used: Linear OR [0.8825,0.8835]; quadratic OR [0.9985,0.9995]. These permit approximate stationary points from -125 to -41; support endpoint is in Table 4.
checks.note: Negative linear and quadratic terms establish concavity of the below index, not necessarily an interior turning point over observed support. Preserve stated H1A support without concluding impossibility from rounded ORs.

checks.calculation: The sum of integer game frequencies through row six divided by game N, times 100, gives 99.6052631579. The printed cumulative percentage is 99.60. However, summing the already-rounded individual row percentages through that row gives exactly 99.60.
